name: Congenital Cataract-Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy-Mitochondrial Myopathy Syndrome
aliases: Congenital Cataract with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy and Mitochondrial Myopathy

criteria.description: Presence of bilateral congenital cataracts detected at birth or early infancy
Echocardiographic evidence of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with left ventricular hypertrophy
Muscle biopsy or biochemical evidence of mitochondrial myopathy including ragged red fibers or respiratory chain enzyme deficiency
Identification of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA or nuclear gene mutations associated with mitochondrial dysfunction
Presence of muscle weakness, exercise intolerance, or cardiomyopathy symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (congenital cataract, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and mitochondrial myopathy) must be met for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by genetic and histopathological findings; no standardized formal criteria exist.

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate levels
Muscle biopsy showing ragged red fibers and cytochrome c oxidase deficiency
Respiratory chain enzyme activity assays demonstrating mitochondrial dysfunction
imaging: Echocardiography revealing hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with asymmetric septal hypertrophy
Brain MRI may show nonspecific white matter changes
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in mitochondrial DNA or nuclear genes affecting mitochondrial function (e.g., mtDNA deletions, POLG mutations)
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities including arrhythmias and conduction defects

distinguishingFeatures: No muscle biopsy evidence of mitochondrial dysfunction

redFlags: Rapid progression of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with heart failure symptoms
Early onset bilateral congenital cataracts with muscle weakness
references: Orphanet: Congenital cataract-hypertrophic cardiomyopathy-mitochondrial myopathy syndrome (ORPHA:1369)
Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy in Mitochondrial Disease, Journal of Cardiology, 2022
